PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS

Items #2 and #5 were not discussed

Item #1 and #4  - The staff made a presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on these items. 

Item #3 - only one matter was discussed.  The staff made a presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on this item.

16.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte provided statistics for the last two weeks regarding crime numbers and arrests made, as well as COPS team assignments overview for the last two weeks. 

Councilmember Garcia asked about homeless encampments. Sergeant Duarte responded that Deputies go to the site, provide resources and information to the homeless individuals, contact Bell Shelter if needed then post a notice to vacate and request relocation. As for the Mixmaster encampment, it is not on the City's property but will be cleared within the next week. 

Mayor Rebollo asked to compare crime and arrest statistics to the previous month. 
 

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction.  




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Councilmember Altamirano asked to pull item #14, and Councilmember Garcia asked to pull item #13 from the Consent Calendar for discussion. 
Item #13 - Councilmember Garcia inquired about how the companies are selected for the on-call list and, once they are approved, how projects are assigned to specific companies. City Manager Cisneros responded that RFP was issued to meet staff augmentation as needed and provide specialized services, and companies were selected based on their qualifications. These companies are invited to participate in RFP for specific projects, and the project is presented to the City Council for approval. 

Councilmember Altamirano moved, seconded by Vice Mayor Argumedo, to adopt a Resolution amending the On-Call Professional Services Agreements by extending terms of agreements through February 1, 2024, with an automatic month-to-month extension for Building and Tenant Improvement Plan Check,  Landscape Architecture,  Park Planning and Design, Planning Services, Environmental Science, Planning, Analysis & Assessment, and Regulatory Compliance, General Civil Engineering, Traffic Engineering,  Real Estate and Right Of Way, Civil Plan Check,  Construction Management & Inspection,  Surveying,  Staff Augmentation, and  Building and Safety. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5) 

Item #14 - Councilmember Altamirano thanked Councilmember Garcia for inviting them to a meeting that provided many ideas about this topic. Councilmember Altamirano had discussions with US Forest Service about affordable housing, and the City would like to bring Gateway Cities on this subject as well. There is an upcoming conference in Oregon that could provide opportunities for affordable housing. City Manager Cisneros added that there is a possibility of exploring affordable housing trust. This partnership with Gateway Cities Housing Trust does not compel the City to support specific projects but only those that the City believes are good. 

In response to Councilmember Garcia on how Board Members would be selected, City Manager Cisneros responded that the Gateway Council of Government Board appoints seven elected members, and the City Council would choose a representative to serve on the Board as the City of Commerce representative. 

Councilmember Argumedo moved, seconded by Councilmember Garcia, to adopt a Resolution approving the City of Commerce’s execution of the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement relating to membership in the Gateway Cities Affordable Housing Trust. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)

19.. Commercial Refuse Hauler Update  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Shelline Katangian, a Key Disposal employee, stated that the company had served commercial customers for over 30 years. With a small number of employees at the company, the customer service provided is outstanding. Ms. Katangian asked that the Key Disposal is added to eight commercial haulers. 

Tom Nitti stated that he represents Key Disposal. Mr. Nitti noted that the previous staff report a couple of years ago included an option that allowed Key Disposal to operate. Still, the current staff report does not have this option. Mr. Nitti also warned about Proposition 218 and other legislation that could lead to litigation. 

John Katangian, Key Disposal, stated that they worked with their customers to bring them to comply with the new law. 

Allan Babashoff has been operating in the City for years. Mr. Babashoff stated that the number of haulers was reduced to 15 and not to eight haulers. Mr. Babashoff also noted that some licenses were transferred and should not be around or allowed. 

Elizabeth Romero, a Key Disposal employee, talked about their customer service and services provided. 

Pedo Ullva spoke for the record. 

Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report and stated that the agreements expire by October 2023. 

According to Acting Director Nila, the City's best interest is to protect the City from mandates and requirements, and there have been more and more regulations. Five years ago, the City received a compliance order, and the City had to address the haulers that were not compliant with orders. RFP was released for semi-exclusive agreements, and the number was limited to eight providers to provide balance and maintain a competitive environment for businesses to choose from. Eight haulers that presented the best proposals were selected, and other haulers received a legal notice to plan their exit from the City five years ago. Haulers that received a five-year notice have until next month to release their customers. 

Further discussion took place on whether legal obligations with the noticing were met. It was also stated that the accounts that would be released by haulers no longer licensed to operate in the City would be picked up by the eight remaining haulers. 

Mayor called a break at 7:44 pm. The City Council returned from a break at 7:59 pm.



20.. Telegraph Corridor Improvements Concept Plan from West City Limit to Atlantic Boulevard Acting Public works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report. Mr. Gibson provided an overview of a traffic study and proposed improvements. According to Mr. Gibson, recommendations and improvements are based on extensive data collection. 
Discussion took place on whether the Mixmaster would be affected by lane merging on Telegraph and how far from the intersection it is recommended. In response to Vice Mayor Argumedo regarding whether the HOV lane would be a good solution for this stretch of Telegraph Rd, Mr. Gilson stated that the traffic flow is not that heavy to justify the HOV lane and also, the cost of it is relatively high. 

Further discussion took place about the turn lane to go to the highway. According to Mr. Gibson, it is a conceptual design, and the conceptual design could be modified to include suggestions and recommendations from the City Council. 

In response to Mayor Rebollo questions about coordinating improvements to Telegraph Road with the County, Acting Director Nila responded that the County reviewed their conceptual design and did not see a significant impact. 
Discussion took place about taking more time for the City Council to review this conceptual design before voting on this item. According to Acting Director Nila, improvements to Telegraph Road would take about six to eight months from approval. Acting Director Nila stated that staff could come back with more visuals for the conceptual design and also identify funding sources for this project. 

No Action was taken on this item; it was a consensus to bring this item back later and provide an opportunity for the City Council to meet with staff. 




21.. Professional Services Agreement for the Preparation of Plans, Specifications, and Engineer’s Estimate for the Sidewalk Improvements on Ferguson Drive  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report. Director Nila explained that outreach was done in late summer or early fall, and residents and businesses affected received a letter/notice. 

Councilmember Lainez asked that staff include Ferguson and Gaspar stop sign design in the project as visibility is not very good. 


18.. Authorize Contract Increase for Exclusive Franchise Agreement with Athens Services for Residential Refuse and Recycling Services and Provide Direction Related to a Potential Second Amendment  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Jim Smith, the Union representative, spoke in support of agenda items #18 and #19. Union Members support the reduction of trash haulers and moving to the more efficient and exclusive or semi-exclusive franchise, and supported the extension of the agreement for additional two years. 

Acting Director of Public Works Nila provided an overview of the item.


23.. Third Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Stantec Architecture, Inc  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo

22.. Approval of the 60% Design Concept for the New Transit Maintenance Facility Project  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Director of Transportation McFerguson provided a brief introduction, and William Todd, Stantec Project Coordinator, provided a presentation. Discussion took place about the 200 visitor and employee dedicated parking spaces, the relatively large lobby area, and the training conference room. According to Director McFerguson, the City could participate in regional area training, host at the City, and rotate hosting with other organizations, which would benefit the City. 

Councilmember Lainez stated that this facility is being built for the future and potential expansion. Director McFerguson added that by applying for federal funding and other funding sources, the City has to justify expansion, ridership, improving connectivity, and present a solid and efficient project. 
In response to Councilmember Garcia's questions about the number of buses, Director McFerguson stated that currently, the City has 40 buses. 



24.. Revisions to the Personnel Classification and Compensation Plan by Amending the Recreation Leader Job Specifications  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo The Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided an overview of the staff report. 

Discussion took place about the challenges staff encountered with hiring Recreation Leaders. Out of 54 candidates, only four were hired for the position. On March 11, 2023, staff will conduct job fair/interviews for multiple Parks and Recreation positions. Staff will be utilizing Facebook, Fun Evening at the Senior Center is planned to promote Parks and Recreation positions and provide an overview of the department. Each household will receive a flyer regarding the upcoming job fair. In response to Councilmember Garcia, whether applicants/participants would be hired on the spot at the Job Fair, Director Alaniz explained that background and medical clearance would be required, but this would cut several weeks of the hiring process. 

Further discussion took place about promotional opportunities for Recreation Aids. Councilmember Garcia inquired whether existing recreation Aids would be qualified for Recreation Leader positions, and Director Alaniz stated that s long they have the required hours, they could apply today. Further discussion took place regarding training for Parks and Recreation Leaders. 


CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia reported that she had a meeting with Assemblywoman Garcia, attended the ICA conference, and Senior Valentine Dance.  

Mayor Rebollo thanked Contract Cities for recognizing a local hero Brandon Tsay who disarmed a mass shooter.  Mayor Reboolo reported that she attended the Contract Cities event for Brandon Tsay's recognition.
